title: How Common Are Common Envelopes? Quantifying Their Role in Forming Gravitational-Wave Sources
comment: Interactive figures and online catalog can be accessed at https://floorbroekgaarden.github.io/Rates_of_Formation_Channels/interactive_figures_and_tables/formation_channel_rates_table.html
summary: A central goal of gravitational-wave astronomy is to use merging binary black hole (BBH), black hole-neutron star (BHNS), and binary neutron star (BNS) systems as fossils to reconstruct the formation and evolution of massive stars across cosmic time. In practice, this inference relies on population-synthesis models that map massive stellar binaries to merging compact objects. However, these models disagree on the dominant orbital-hardening mechanisms within isolated binary evolution, particularly on whether common-envelope (CE) evolution is required. To address this, we compile and systematically compare formation-channel predictions from more than 200 isolated-binary population-synthesis simulations, organized within a unified hierarchical taxonomy. We find that BBH and BHNS formation pathways span nearly the full allowed range from CE-dominated to without-CE-dominated evolution (0-100%), while often predicting similar merger rates, revealing a fundamental degeneracy: merger-rate measurements alone do not uniquely constrain the underlying evolutionary pathways. In contrast, BNS formation proceeds almost exclusively through channels involving at least one CE phase (>90-100%), suggesting CE evolution plays a qualitatively different role in BNS than in BBH and BHNS formation. The relative contributions of with-CE and without-CE pathways are governed primarily by assumptions controlling mass-transfer stability, angular-momentum loss, CE efficiency, and supernova physics, which often act non-linearly and in correlated fashion, such that trends from one-at-a-time parameter variations do not generalize across simulation frameworks. Robust interpretation of gravitational-wave populations will therefore require transparent formation-channel definitions, reproducible analysis pipelines, systematic cross-code comparisons, and observational constraints that extend beyond merger rates alone.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically compares over 200 isolated-binary population-synthesis simulations, finding that BBH and BHNS formation pathways range from 0-100% CE-dominated while predicting similar merger rates, revealing a fundamental degeneracy. In contrast, BNS formation requires at least one CE phase (>90-100%). The authors conclude that robust interpretation of gravitational-wave populations requires transparent definitions, reproducible pipelines, cross-code comparisons, and constraints beyond merger rates alone.
AI.motivation: To determine whether common-envelope (CE) evolution is necessary for forming merging compact objects (BBH, BHNS, BNS), and to resolve disagreements between population-synthesis models on the dominant orbital-hardening mechanisms within isolated binary evolution.
AI.method: Compiled and systematically compared formation-channel predictions from over 200 isolated-binary population-synthesis simulations, organized within a unified hierarchical taxonomy, analyzing the role of CE evolution across different compact-object merger types.
AI.result: BBH and BHNS pathways span 0-100% CE-dominated evolution while predicting similar merger rates, revealing a fundamental degeneracy. BNS formation proceeds almost exclusively through channels involving at least one CE phase (>90-100%). Key governing assumptions include mass-transfer stability, angular-momentum loss, CE efficiency, and supernova physics, which act non-linearly and in correlated fashion.
AI.conclusion: Merger-rate measurements alone cannot uniquely constrain evolutionary pathways. Robust interpretation of gravitational-wave populations requires transparent formation-channel definitions, reproducible analysis pipelines, systematic cross-code comparisons, and additional observational constraints beyond merger rates.

title: Mapping Active Star-Formation in Serpens and the Aquila Rift
summary: We report the results of a high-sensitivity survey for Herbig-Haro (HH) outflows in the Serpens-Aquila Rift using the DECam instrument on the 4-meter telescope. We have detected 88 new HH objects, more than tripling the total known in this region. We have also identified likely progenitors for most of these outflows. By combining HH object and progenitor locations with literature dust maps and Gaia astrometry, we find that HH objects mark five spatially distinct clouds hosting active star formation: the Serpens Molecular Cloud and LDN 673 at 400-500 pc, the more distant West and East components of the Aquila Rift at ~600 and 700 pc, respectively, and a near cloud in Serpens at ~250 pc. In both the Serpens Molecular Cloud and the Western Aquila Rift, HH objects broadly trace gas structures on the edges of low-density cavities surrounding known stellar populations, consistent with active star formation in feedback-driven shells. The near cloud in Serpens is not associated with any established stellar population, but its position and velocity suggest that it is part of the Local Bubble. And the HH objects there may mark the start of a new stellar generation connected to the Scutum North Association. Our Herbig-Haro objects therefore serve as a powerful indicator of star formation sites even in the absence of astrometrically characterized young stars, making them a useful tool for guiding future YSO surveys.

AI.tldr: A DECam survey of the Serpens-Aquila Rift detected 88 new Herbig-Haro objects (tripling known counts), identified their progenitors, and revealed five distinct star-forming clouds at different distances (250–700 pc). HH objects trace feedback-driven cavities and even pinpoint a previously unknown star-forming region in the Local Bubble, demonstrating their utility for guiding future YSO surveys.
AI.motivation: To conduct a high-sensitivity survey for Herbig-Haro outflows in the Serpens-Aquila Rift to discover new star formation sites and understand the region's cloud structures and dynamics.
AI.method: Wide-field imaging survey using DECam on the 4-meter telescope, combined with literature dust maps and Gaia astrometry to identify HH objects, their progenitors, and associate them with cloud structures at different distances.
AI.result: 88 new HH objects detected (tripling known total), five distinct star-forming clouds identified at distances of ~250, 400-500, ~600, and ~700 pc. HH objects trace gas on edges of low-density cavities in feedback-driven shells. A near (~250 pc) Serpens cloud is part of the Local Bubble, possibly linked to the Scutum North Association.
AI.conclusion: Herbig-Haro objects are powerful tracers of star formation even without astrometrically characterized young stars, making them a valuable tool for directing future YSO surveys.

title: Joint Multi-Period Fermi-LAT and LHAASO Constraints on Axion-Like Particles from Mrk 421 Using Profile Likelihood with Gaussian Copula Correlation
comment: Ready to submit; comments are welcome
summary: We construct a multi-epoch joint profile-likelihood framework to constrain axion-like particles (ALPs), employing a Gaussian copula ($ρ=0.03$) to account for weak correlations among distinct observational periods. Different from traditional independent likelihood addition, our scheme globally optimizes nuisance parameters under the no-ALP hypothesis prior to profiling ALP mass $m_a$ and coupling $g_{aγ}$, enhancing numerical stability and statistical consistency. Using five sets of simultaneous Fermi-LAT and LHAASO data of Mrk 421, we implement both two-zone hybrid and single-zone hadronic jet models. In the CAST-sensitive low-mass regime $m_a\lesssim1$ neV, the 95\% CL upper limit of $g_{aγ}$ is $8.33\times10^{-14}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. Over $0.1$-$500$ neV, conservative bounds read $g_{aγ}<6.50\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ (two-zone) and $g_{aγ}<7.30\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ (single-zone). These results benefit from LHAASO's broadband very high energy coverage and long term monitoring of Mrk 421; the developed framework provides a robust and scalable pipeline suitable for future multi-messenger ALP searches with next-generation gamma-ray observatories.

AI.tldr: The authors develop a multi-epoch joint profile-likelihood framework using a Gaussian copula (ρ=0.03) to constrain axion-like particles (ALPs) from Mrk 421 data. They derive 95% CL upper limits on g_aγ: 8.33×10⁻¹⁴ GeV⁻¹ for m_a≲1 neV (CAST-sensitive regime), and conservative bounds of <6.50×10⁻¹² GeV⁻¹ (two-zone) and <7.30×10⁻¹² GeV⁻¹ (single-zone) over 0.1-500 neV.
AI.motivation: To improve upon traditional independent likelihood addition for ALP constraints by introducing a copula-based joint framework that accounts for weak inter-epoch correlations and globally optimizes nuisance parameters under the no-ALP hypothesis.
AI.method: Multi-epoch joint profile-likelihood with Gaussian copula (ρ=0.03); global nuisance parameter optimization under no-ALP hypothesis prior to profiling m_a and g_aγ; applied to five sets of simultaneous Fermi-LAT and LHAASO observations of Mrk 421 using two-zone hybrid and single-zone hadronic jet models.
AI.result: 95% CL upper limit g_aγ=8.33×10⁻¹⁴ GeV⁻¹ for m_a≲1 neV (CAST regime); over 0.1-500 neV: g_aγ<6.50×10⁻¹² GeV⁻¹ (two-zone) and <7.30×10⁻¹² GeV⁻¹ (single-zone).
AI.conclusion: LHAASO's broadband VHE coverage and long-term Mrk 421 monitoring enhance ALP constraints; the framework provides a robust, scalable pipeline for future multi-messenger ALP searches with next-generation gamma-ray observatories.

title: The X-ray emission of the long-period transient and accreting cataclysmic variable ASKAP J174508.9-505149
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A Letters on 27/05/2026. 7 pages (4 main text+ 3 appendices)
summary: Long-period transients (LPTs) challenge our knowledge of the mechanism producing radio periodic pulsations in compact objects. Some LPTs have been associated with systems hosting a white dwarf and a low-mass star in a detached binary. Recently, a new LPT (ASKAP\,J174508.9-505149) has been classified as an accreting cataclysmic variable (CV). In the present letter, we report on the detailed study of the X-ray variability of ASKAP\,J174508.9-505149 as observed by \emph{XMM-Newton} and \emph{Einstein Probe} between September 2025 and May 2026. Simultaneous optical and radio observations are also presented. We studied the timing variability of the source, and estimated an X-ray periodicity of $P=4868(22)$\,s, consistent with radio and optical periods. We also observe the same periodicity in the hardness ratio extracted from the \emph{XMM-Newton} observation, peaking at the minimum of the modulation. A long-term modulation is also present in the X-rays and in the B-band photometry, but it is poorly constrained by the current dataset. Spectral X-ray analysis shows the presence of a black-body component ($\sim$0.1\,keV), a collisionally ionised plasma ($\sim$15\,keV), and an absorption feature at 0.77 keV (possibly due to Oxygen-VII). This is the third LPT detected in the X-ray band, the second with a detected X-ray periodicity and variable X-ray emission, and the first conclusively recognised as an accreting magnetic CV.

AI.tldr: The paper reports a detailed X-ray variability study of the long-period transient ASKAP J174508.9-505149 using XMM-Newton and Einstein Probe data (Sep 2025–May 2026), finding an X-ray periodicity of ~4868 s consistent with radio/optical periods, a hardness ratio modulation, spectral components including a blackbody (~0.1 keV), hot plasma (~15 keV), and an O-VII absorption feature. It is the third LPT detected in X-rays, the second with a detected X-ray periodicity, and the first conclusively identified as an accreting magnetic cataclysmic variable.
AI.motivation: Long-period transients (LPTs) challenge the standard understanding of radio periodic pulsations from compact objects. This study aims to characterize the X-ray variability of ASKAP J174508.9-505149, a newly discovered LPT classified as a cataclysmic variable, to confirm its nature and identify its physical mechanisms.
AI.method: The authors analyzed timing and spectral X-ray data from XMM-Newton and Einstein Probe (Sep 2025–May 2026), combined with simultaneous optical and radio observations. They extracted X-ray periodicity via timing analysis, computed hardness ratios, modeled the X-ray spectrum with multiple components, and searched for long-term modulations in X-ray and B-band photometry.
AI.result: An X-ray periodicity of P=4868(22) s was measured, consistent with radio and optical periods. The same periodicity appears in the hardness ratio, peaking at the modulation minimum. Long-term modulation is present but poorly constrained. The X-ray spectrum is composed of a ~0.1 keV blackbody, a ~15 keV collisionally ionized plasma, and an absorption feature at 0.77 keV (likely O-VII).
AI.conclusion: ASKAP J174508.9-505149 is the third LPT detected in X-rays, the second with a detected X-ray periodicity and variable X-ray emission, and the first conclusively recognized as an accreting magnetic cataclysmic variable. This establishes magnetic CVs as a viable class for producing LPTs.

title: Modeling Gamma-Ray Burst Spectra with Convolutional Neural Networks: Fast-Cooling Synchrotron Emission in a Decaying Magnetic Field
comment: 20 pages, 9 figures,accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: The radiation mechanism of gamma-ray burst (GRB) prompt emission remains uncertain. Although the fast-cooling synchrotron model in a decaying magnetic field can account for the characteristic nonthermal spectral shape, its computational cost has limited its use in systematic observational fitting and statistical model comparison. We develop a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based spectral emulator for this physical model and train it on a large synthetic data set generated over a physically motivated parameter space. The trained network reproduces the numerical spectra with high fidelity while reducing the cost of spectral evaluation to the millisecond level. We then incorporate the emulator into a Bayesian spectral-analysis framework and apply it to the time-resolved spectra of GRB 231020A observed by Fermi/GBM. In most time intervals, the decaying-field fast-cooling synchrotron model provides better fits and smaller Bayesian information criterion values than the standard fast-cooling synchrotron model. These results suggest that a radially decaying magnetic field provides a plausible and more physically motivated interpretation of the prompt-emission spectrum of this burst, while also indicating that the emulator offers a practical route for large-sample Bayesian inference and systematic comparisons of GRB prompt-emission models.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a CNN-based spectral emulator for the fast-cooling synchrotron model with a decaying magnetic field, reducing evaluation time to milliseconds. Applied to GRB 231020A Fermi/GBM data via Bayesian analysis, the decaying-field model outperforms the standard synchrotron model, demonstrating a practical path for large-sample GRB prompt-emission model comparison.
AI.motivation: The radiation mechanism of GRB prompt emission is uncertain; the fast-cooling synchrotron model in a decaying magnetic field explains the nonthermal spectral shape but is computationally too expensive for systematic fitting and statistical comparison.
AI.method: A convolutional neural network (CNN)-based spectral emulator is trained on a large synthetic dataset over a physically motivated parameter space. The emulator is then embedded into a Bayesian spectral-analysis framework to fit time-resolved spectra of GRB 231020A observed by Fermi/GBM.
AI.result: The CNN emulator reproduces numerical spectra with high fidelity and reduces spectral evaluation cost to milliseconds. For GRB 231020A, the decaying-field fast-cooling synchrotron model yields better fits and smaller Bayesian information criterion values than the standard fast-cooling synchrotron model in most time intervals.
AI.conclusion: A radially decaying magnetic field offers a plausible, more physically motivated interpretation of GRB prompt-emission spectra. The emulator enables practical large-sample Bayesian inference and systematic comparisons of GRB prompt-emission models.

title: Simulations of interaction between outflow and surrounding broken power-law circumnuclear medium: implications for different radio light curves of TDEs
summary: The complex radio light curves of tidal disruption events (TDEs) challenge our understanding of the properties of both the outflows and the circumnuclear medium (CNM) surrounding supermassive black holes. In this work, we explore outflow-CNM interactions across a broad parameter space using three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations, adopting a broken power-law CNM density profile with a transition near the Bondi radius. The outflow-CNM interaction inside Bondi radius produces an early radio flare (\(\lesssim 2\) yr) once the emitting region becomes optically thin. A second radio rebrightening can appear a few years later if the outflow decelerates beyond Bondi radius. We also find that either a very dense inner CNM, which causes rapid deceleration, or a rarefied outer CNM suppresses the late rebrightening that will produces a single early-peaked flare. In contrast, a rarefied CNM inside the Bondi radius suppresses the early flare and yields a single late-peaked event. For the case of very dense CNM at large radii, the interaction will trigger a sharp late-time rise as observed in some TDEs. We further explore the interaction of a relativistic jet with a broken power-law CNM, which can reproduce the characteristic light curves as observed in jetted TDEs without invoking complex jet structure.

AI.tldr: This paper uses 3D hydrodynamic simulations to study how outflows from tidal disruption events interact with the circumnuclear medium around supermassive black holes. The interaction produces distinct radio light curve features—early flares (within ~2 years from inside Bondi radius), late rebrightening (from outside Bondi radius), or single-peaked events—depending on the CNM density profile. The model also reproduces observed light curves of jetted TDEs without requiring complex jet structure.
AI.motivation: Complex radio light curves of tidal disruption events challenge our understanding of outflow properties and the circumnuclear medium surrounding supermassive black holes.
AI.method: Three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations exploring outflow-CNM interactions across a broad parameter space, adopting a broken power-law CNM density profile with a transition near the Bondi radius.
AI.result: Outflow-CNM interaction inside Bondi radius produces an early radio flare (≲2 yr); a second radio rebrightening can appear later if outflow decelerates beyond Bondi radius. Very dense inner CNM or rarefied outer CNM suppresses late rebrightening (single early-peaked flare). Rarefied inner CNM suppresses early flare (single late-peaked event). Very dense outer CNM triggers sharp late-time rise. Relativistic jet with broken power-law CNM reproduces characteristic light curves of jetted TDEs.
AI.conclusion: The diversity of TDE radio light curves can be explained by varying the CNM density profile shape, without invoking complex outflow or jet structures.

title: Detectability of secondary images from flares near Sgr A* with mock GRAVITY data
summary: The orbital motion of near-infrared flares reported by the GRAVITY collaboration encodes information about both the dynamics of accretion matter and the underlying spacetime geometry. The centroid track of these flares, which corresponds to the flux-weighted center of light, incorporates contributions from primary, secondary and higher-order images. Thus, it potentially indicates distinctive signatures of the spacetime geometry, even when these individual multiple images remain unresolved. In this study, we explore the detectability of the secondary images from flares orbiting Sgr A* through mock data simulating future GRAVITY observations. Specifically, we compare the model in which the centroid coincides with the track of the primary images with another model in which the centroid incorporates flux-weighted contributions from both the primary and secondary images. Fitting these models to the mock data based on Bayesian framework, we quantify the conditions under which the signature of secondary images can be statistically distinguishable. We demonstrate that increasing the sample size by an order of magnitude alone could not yield strong evidence for distinguishing the secondary image. Robust detectability ($|Δ\text{BIC}| >7.9$) is achieved when both with the improved sample size and astrometric uncertainties reduced to 40\% of current uncertainties of GRAVITY astrometric data. Unlike the primary image, which is dominated by accretion flow physics, the secondary images originate from gravitational lensing in the strong-field regime. Their detection is an essential first step toward probing higher-order images and the photon rings.

AI.tldr: This study simulates future GRAVITY observations to determine whether secondary images (gravitationally lensed) of flares orbiting Sgr A* can be statistically distinguished from primary images. Using Bayesian model comparison on mock centroid track data, the authors find that robust detectability (|ΔBIC| > 7.9) requires both an order-of-magnitude increase in sample size and a 60% reduction in astrometric uncertainties. This detection is a critical step toward probing higher-order images and photon rings.
AI.motivation: The centroid tracks of near-infrared flares from Sgr A* observed by GRAVITY contain contributions from primary, secondary, and higher-order images, potentially encoding signatures of strong-field spacetime geometry. Detecting secondary images would provide a first step toward probing gravitational lensing effects and photon rings, but it is unclear whether current or near-future observations can statistically distinguish these contributions.
AI.method: Mock data simulating future GRAVITY observations of flares orbiting Sgr A* are generated. Two models are compared via Bayesian framework: (1) centroid track = primary image only, (2) centroid track = flux-weighted sum of primary + secondary images. Model comparison uses ΔBIC (Bayesian Information Criterion) to quantify distinguishability under varying sample sizes and astrometric uncertainties.
AI.result: Increasing sample size by an order of magnitude alone is insufficient for robust detection. Robust detectability (|ΔBIC| > 7.9) requires both a 10× larger sample size and astrometric uncertainties reduced to 40% of current GRAVITY levels.
AI.conclusion: Detecting secondary images is essential for probing higher-order images and photon rings, but requires substantial improvements in both sample size and astrometric precision beyond current GRAVITY capabilities.

title: The quenching time and timescale distribution of z~2 quiescent galaxies from precise colour distribution analysis
comment: Submitted to OJA, comments welcome. Code will be made available on acceptance
summary: Understanding when and how galaxies quench their star formation is crucial for understanding the dominant physical processes at play. The spectral energy distribution (SED) of galaxies encodes significant information on their past histories: the relative importance of different physical processes influences the observed distribution of SED shapes in the galaxy population. We use a simulation based inference (SBI) approach to directly constrain the distribution of formation times, quenching times and quenching timescales within the massive galaxy population at z >~ 2 from their broad band photometric colour distribution at 1.7<z<2. We demonstrate that a simple distribution of double power-law star formation histories accurately fits the distribution of SED shapes of galaxies with log10(M*/Msol)>10.3. We measure a quenched galaxy fraction of 0.24+/-0.02, with the number density of quenched galaxies rising rapidly 2.5Gyr after the Big Bang (z<~2.6). Galaxies must quench rapidly to achieve the precise bimodal colour distribution: defining the quenching timescale as the time from peak star formation rate (SFR_peak) -> 0.5xSFR_peak, the quenching timescale distribution has a mode at 97_{-25}^{+31}Myr, a median of 182+/-16Myr and a tail to ~700Myr. To achieve full quiescence takes a median time of ~400Myr. Comparing to direct number density measurements of quenched galaxies at z>2 the combination of recent and rapid quenching inferred from the fossil record suggests a substantial rejuvenation and/or merger rate for quenched galaxies observed directly at z>3.5.

AI.tldr: Using simulation-based inference on broad-band photometry of massive galaxies at 1.7<z<2, this paper constrains their star formation histories—finding rapid quenching (median ~182 Myr) and a quenched fraction of 0.24, with indications of rejuvenation/mergers for high-z quenched galaxies.
AI.motivation: To understand when and how galaxies quench star formation by directly constraining the distributions of formation times, quenching times, and quenching timescales in massive galaxies at z>~2.
AI.method: Simulation-based inference (SBI) applied to broad-band photometric color distributions (1.7<z<2) to fit a double power-law star formation history model for galaxies with log10(M*/Msol)>10.3.
AI.result: Quenched fraction of 0.24±0.02; quenching timescale mode ~97 Myr, median ~182 Myr, tail to ~700 Myr; full quiescence median ~400 Myr; rapid rise of quenched number density after 2.5 Gyr (z<~2.6).
AI.conclusion: Massive galaxies quench rapidly (≲200 Myr), but comparison with direct observations at z>3.5 suggests substantial rejuvenation and/or mergers are needed to reconcile the fossil-record inference with observed number densities.

title: The Multi-phase Biconical Outflow in the local IR-Luminous Merger IRASF01364-1042
comment: 23 pages, 16 figures, accepted for publication in A & A
summary: We investigate the spatially-resolved ISM properties of the local ($z = 0.048$), IR-luminous ($L_{\rm IR} = 10^{11.87}$\,L$_\odot$), late-stage galaxy merger IRAS F01364-1042, combining multi-wavelength IFU observations from \textit{JWST/MIRI-MRS}, ALMA and Keck/KCWI. Using these datasets, we construct emission line maps of several key tracers of the ionized (e.g., [Ne\,II]\,12.8$μ$m, [O\,III]$\lambda5007$), warm molecular (e.g., \ce{H2}\,0-0\,S(3)), and cold molecular gas (e.g., CO (J$=2-1$)), and perform detailed decomposition of spectra extracted in resolved regions across the areas of emission. We confirm the presence of a multi-phase galactic biconical outflow along the minor axis of a highly inclined rotating disk. The inferred outflow velocities are $\sim\,$500 - 600\,km\,s$^{-1}$ $\sim\,$350\,km\,s$^{-1}$, and $\sim\,$200 - 300\,km\,s$^{-1}$, in the ionized, warm and cold molecular phase, respectively, with corresponding mass outflow rates of $\sim 0.3 - 2.3$, $\sim 31$, and $\sim 38 - 240$\,M$_\odot\,$yr$^{-1}$. The cold molecular phase dominates both the total mass outflow rate and the associated kinetic energy ($\sim\,2 - 8 \times 10^{42}$\,erg\,s$^{-1}$). We confirm, for the first time, a dust-obscured AGN in IRAS\,F01364-1042, via detection of the [Ne\,V]\,14.3$μ$m line. The low inferred AGN bolometric luminosity ($1.2 - 1.8 \times 10^{43}$\,erg\,s$^{-1}$) suggests that the nuclear starburst alone, with a star formation rate of $\sim 40 - 60$\,M$_\odot$\,yr$^{-1}$, can account for the energy required to drive the outflow, though a more active AGN phase in the recent past may have also played a role. Our work showcases the necessity of multi-wavelength observations for interpreting the gas dynamics in merger-driven dusty starbursts, and the capability of \textit{JWST/MIRI-MRS} to uncover obscured, low-luminosity AGN that may be common in these systems.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the multi-phase ISM properties of the local luminous galaxy merger IRAS F01364-1042 using JWST/MIRI-MRS, ALMA, and Keck/KCWI. It reveals a multi-phase biconical outflow dominated by cold molecular gas, detects a dust-obscured AGN via [Ne V] emission, and finds the nuclear starburst likely powers the outflow.
AI.motivation: To understand the spatially-resolved ISM properties and gas dynamics in merger-driven dusty starbursts, and to demonstrate the necessity of multi-wavelength observations for such systems.
AI.method: Combined multi-wavelength IFU observations from JWST/MIRI-MRS (mid-IR), ALMA (mm), and Keck/KCWI (optical); constructed emission line maps of ionized, warm molecular, and cold molecular gas tracers; performed spectral decomposition in resolved regions across the emission areas.
AI.result: Confirmed a multi-phase galactic biconical outflow along the minor axis with velocities: ionized ~500-600 km/s, warm molecular ~350 km/s, cold molecular ~200-300 km/s. Mass outflow rates: ionized ~0.3-2.3, warm molecular ~31, cold molecular ~38-240 M☉/yr. Cold molecular phase dominates mass and kinetic energy (~2-8×10^42 erg/s). Detected [Ne V] 14.3μm confirming a dust-obscured AGN with low bolometric luminosity (1.2-1.8×10^43 erg/s). Nuclear starburst (SFR ~40-60 M☉/yr) can account for outflow energetics.
AI.conclusion: Multi-wavelength observations are essential for interpreting gas dynamics in merger-driven dusty starbursts. JWST/MIRI-MRS can uncover obscured low-luminosity AGN that may be common in such systems. The cold molecular phase dominates outflow energetics, and the starburst likely powers the outflow, though a past AGN phase may have contributed.

title: A high-energy neutrino flare associated with nearby bright interacting supernova SN 2021foa
summary: While core-collapse supernovae have been widely discussed as potential neutrino sources, definitive observational evidence has remained elusive. In this work, we report evidence of high-energy neutrino emission in the direction of supernova SN 2021foa, which is one of the closest and brightest interacting supernovae observed to date. Using the second data release of muon track data from the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, we conducted a time-dependent analysis and identified a neutrino clustering that temporally coincides with the optical peak of SN 2021foa, occurring approximately 16 to 22 days after the discovery date, with a maximum test statistic of $\sim 28.2$. Monte Carlo simulations indicate that the probability of observing such a neutrino excess by chance is $\sim6.7 \times 10^{-5}$, corresponding to a significance of $\sim4.0\,σ$. The spatial and temporal correlation strongly suggests that the neutrinos originate from the supernova. SN 2021foa is a unique "flip-flop" supernova; its spectra repeatedly transitioned between hydrogen-rich (Type IIn) and helium-rich (Type Ibn) phases within 50 days post-peak, reflecting a violent and complex mass-loss history of its progenitor. The inferred neutrino energy exceeds the optical radiative energy and ejecta kinetic energy of the supernova by orders of magnitude, suggesting that the neutrino emission is likely powered by a delayed central engine driving a jet that is choked within the dense circumstellar medium.

AI.tldr: IceCube detected high-energy neutrinos from SN 2021foa, a unique "flip-flop" supernova, at ~4.0σ significance coinciding with its optical peak (16-22 days post-discovery). The neutrino energy exceeds optical and kinetic energies by orders of magnitude, suggesting a delayed central engine driving a choked jet.
AI.motivation: Core-collapse supernovae are potential neutrino sources, but definitive observational evidence has been elusive; this work aims to establish such evidence using IceCube data.
AI.method: Time-dependent analysis of IceCube's second muon track data release, targeting SN 2021foa; Monte Carlo simulations to assess significance.
AI.result: Neutrino clustering coinciding with optical peak (16-22 days post-discovery), test statistic ~28.2, significance ~4.0σ (p~6.7×10⁻⁵). Neutrino energy exceeds optical radiative and ejecta kinetic energy by orders of magnitude.
AI.conclusion: The spatial and temporal correlation strongly suggests neutrinos originate from SN 2021foa, likely powered by a delayed central engine driving a choked jet within the dense circumstellar medium.

title: Analytic insight into the physics of SASI II. Spiral instability of the prograde mode in a rotating stellar core
summary: During the core-collapse of a rotating massive star, the standing accretion shock instability (SASI) favours the development of non-axisymmetric motions which can imprint specific frequency signatures on the neutrino and gravitational wave signals.This study establishes analytical approximations for the eigenfrequencies of the dominant SASI modes. It also explains the physical mechanism responsible for the further destabilization of prograde SASI modes by differential rotation. A perturbative analysis is used to calculate the eigenfrequencies of a stalled accretion shock in spherical geometry, taking into account the rotation of the collapsing stellar core. The formulation of the perturbative equations as a self-forced oscillator is extended to include differential rotation and interpret the results physically. The oscillation frequency of the dominant mode weakly depends on the detailed formulation of neutrino emission if the shock radius exceeds ~1.5 times the radius r_nabla of maximum deceleration. Analytical expressions are obtained for the one and two-armed spiral modes with a 10% accuracy in this regime. The effect of differential rotation is explained by the role of phase mixing between the advective forcing and the acoustic structure. The radial wavelength of vorticity perturbations associated with the prograde mode is increased by differential rotation, leading to a better phase match with the large radial scale of the acoustic structure. Even when rotation is too modest to involve a corotation radius, its adverse effect on phase mixing can be significant at small radius due to the steep inward increase of the rotation frequency ~1/r^2 in the region of stationary accretion. In the regime of stronger rotation involving a corotation radius, the stationary phase approximation sheds light on the dominant advective-acoustic coupling, located between the corotation zone and the shock.

AI.tldr: This paper develops analytical models for the eigenfrequencies of the standing accretion shock instability (SASI) in rotating core-collapse supernovae, showing that differential rotation destabilizes prograde modes by improving phase matching between advective forcing and acoustic structure, with analytical expressions accurate to 10% for spiral modes when the shock radius exceeds ~1.5 times the deceleration radius.
AI.motivation: To understand the role of rotation in destabilizing non-axisymmetric SASI modes during core-collapse supernovae, and to provide analytical approximations for the eigenfrequencies that can be linked to observable neutrino and gravitational wave signals.
AI.method: Perturbative analysis of stalled accretion shock eigenfrequencies in spherical geometry with rotation, extending a self-forced oscillator formulation to include differential rotation, and employing stationary phase approximation for regimes with corotation radius.
AI.result: Analytical expressions for one- and two-armed spiral mode frequencies with ~10% accuracy when shock radius > 1.5 r_nabla; differential rotation increases radial wavelength of vorticity perturbations in prograde modes, improving phase matching with acoustic structure; phase mixing effects can be significant even without corotation due to steep ~1/r^2 rotation profile.
AI.conclusion: Rotation destabilizes prograde SASI modes via phase mixing mechanisms, and the dominant mode frequency depends weakly on neutrino emission details in the applicable regime, enabling robust analytical predictions.

title: A New Member of the Fast and Furious Family: A Relativistic and Time-Variable UV Outflow in a Luminous Quasar
comment: 40 pages, 12 figures, 10 tables, published in the Astrophysical Journal
summary: We report the fastest quasar outflow first detected in the ultraviolet, via variable C IV and Si IV absorption at outflow velocities $-77,000$ km s$^{-1}$ to at least $-90,000$ km s$^{-1}$, in the radio-quiet quasar SDSS J231854.31+243954.2 (J2318). J2318 is a weak-lined quasar in the rest-frame ultraviolet, but Gemini GNIRS spectroscopy reveals an H$α$ redshift of $z=2.6781\pm0.0004$. A twenty-year photometric time series shows peak-to-peak variability of 0.5 mag in the $g$ band. The C IV outflow strengthened monotonically over three epochs spanning $\sim$2.2 rest-frame years. The existence of such a high-velocity outflow implies that models of quasar outflows must be able to either accelerate gas to $0.3c$ while still preserving C IV and Si IV ions, or enable the formation of C IV and Si IV ions in gas which has been accelerated to $0.3c$. Virial estimates reveal a black-hole mass of $1.65\times10^9~M_\odot$, which leads to an Eddington luminosity and Eddington ratio of $2.4\times10^{47}$ erg s$^{-1}$ and $0.45$, respectively. Using very conservative assumptions, the UV-absorbing outflow alone has an estimated mass loss of $>0.82~M_\odot~{\rm yr}^{-1}$ and a kinetic luminosity ratio $L_{kin}/L_{bol}\geq0.75$%. The lower limit is just above the threshold usually cited for significant feedback on the host galaxy. Comparison to PDS 456, the only other known quasar with a UV-absorbing outflow at $0.3c$, suggests that the true $\dot{M}$ and $L_{kin}/L_{bol}$ could be up to two orders of magnitude larger.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the fastest ultraviolet-detected quasar outflow in SDSS J231854.31+243954.2, with C IV and Si IV absorption at velocities of -77,000 to -90,000 km/s (0.3c). The outflow strengthened over ~2.2 rest-frame years. The quasar has a black hole mass of 1.65×10⁹ M⊙, Eddington ratio of 0.45, and the outflow alone has mass loss >0.82 M⊙/yr and kinetic luminosity ratio ≥0.75%, exceeding the feedback threshold.
AI.motivation: To characterize the fastest known UV-detected quasar outflow and assess its potential for feedback on the host galaxy, as only one other quasar (PDS 456) is known to have a UV-absorbing outflow at 0.3c.
AI.method: UV spectroscopy (variable C IV and Si IV absorption lines), Gemini GNIRS spectroscopy for Hα redshift, twenty-year photometric time series for variability, and virial black hole mass estimation.
AI.result: Discovered outflow at -77,000 to -90,000 km/s (0.3c) that strengthened over three epochs. Black hole mass 1.65×10⁹ M⊙, Eddington luminosity 2.4×10⁴⁷ erg/s, Eddington ratio 0.45. Outflow mass loss >0.82 M⊙/yr, Lkin/Lbol ≥ 0.75%.
AI.conclusion: The outflow surpasses the threshold for significant feedback on the host galaxy, and comparison with PDS 456 suggests true values could be orders of magnitude larger, implying models must explain acceleration to 0.3c while preserving C IV and Si IV ions.

title: Bar-induced deflection of open cluster tidal tails
summary: We present a systematic study of how the Galactic bar affects the orientation of tidal tails of open clusters and assess the power of tail morphology to constrain the bar's pattern speed. Using test-particle simulations, we follow the evolution of $\sim 1450$ observed open clusters from the Hunt & Reffert (2024) catalogue in an axisymmetric reference potential and in eight barred potentials with pattern speeds ranging from $Ω_b = 20$ km/s/kpc to $Ω_b = 55$ km/s/kpc. We quantify the bar effect through the deflection angle -- the rotation of the tail orientation in the barred model relative to the axisymmetric case. The deflection angle varies systematically with bar pattern speed and cluster guiding radius. The largest deflections occur for clusters near the outer Lindblad resonance (OLR), with the sign of the angle set by the orientation of the orbit's pericentre relative to the bar's major axis. For each cluster we measure the distance from the centre beyond which different bar models produce distinguishable tail orientations, and classify each cluster as bar-sensitive or bar-insensitive based on its maximum absolute deflection across the bar models. Comparing with observed tidal tails from the literature, we find that the extended tails of NGC 2632 and the Hyades disfavour moderate pattern speeds. We provide a catalogue of deflection angles, minimal tail extents, and bar-sensitivity flags to guide future observational searches and the re-assessment of existing tidal tail catalogues.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how the Milky Way's bar affects tidal tails of open clusters, using simulations of 1450 clusters with different bar pattern speeds. The deflection angle of tails correlates with bar speed and cluster position, especially near the outer Lindblad resonance. Observed tails of NGC 2632 and Hyades disfavor moderate pattern speeds. A catalogue of deflection angles and sensitivity flags is provided for future studies.
AI.motivation: To systematically study how the Galactic bar influences the orientation of tidal tails of open clusters, and to assess whether tail morphology can constrain the bar's pattern speed.
AI.method: Test-particle simulations of ~1450 observed open clusters from the Hunt & Reffert (2024) catalogue in an axisymmetric reference potential and eight barred potentials with pattern speeds from Ω_b = 20 to 55 km/s/kpc. Quantified bar effect via deflection angle (rotation of tail orientation relative to axisymmetric case). Classified clusters as bar-sensitive or bar-insensitive based on maximum absolute deflection.
AI.result: Deflection angle varies systematically with bar pattern speed and cluster guiding radius. Largest deflections occur near the outer Lindblad resonance (OLR), with sign set by pericentre orientation relative to bar's major axis. Extended tails of NGC 2632 and the Hyades disfavor moderate pattern speeds. A catalogue of deflection angles, minimal tail extents, and bar-sensitivity flags is produced.
AI.conclusion: Tidal tail morphology of open clusters is a promising diagnostic for constraining the Galactic bar's pattern speed, with specific clusters identified as particularly sensitive probes.

title: Research Note: Ghostly DLAs in SDSS DR16
summary:
In Petitjean (2026, arXiv:2605.12188)), we revisited the origin of proximate damped Lyman-alpha absorbers (PDLAs), which trace cold gas within 3000 km/s of the quasar redshift, and interpreted their kinematics and physical properties within a unified framework. We showed that most PDLAs are associated with the environment of the AGN and/or the quasar host galaxy. We also provided the first census and characterization of absorption systems exhibiting strong absorption from excited levels of atomic ground states among quasar-associated absorbers. Among these, ghostly and coronagraphic systems arise in dense, compact gas that partially covers the quasar emission regions. Most systems are associated with outflows reaching velocities up to -2000 km/s, while a smaller fraction of inflowing clouds extends to velocities of up to +1200 km/s.
  In the present work, we provide an updated classification of PDLAs, including a revised catalogue of ghostly systems that more than doubles the number of previously known detections. We investigate the properties of these systems by measuring and discussing the equivalent widths of the detected absorption lines in both stacked spectra and individual ghostly systems. In particular, we show that although most ghostly systems are bona fide DLAs, this is not always the case.

AI.tldr: This paper updates the classification of PDLAs, with a revised catalogue of ghostly systems (more than doubling known detections), and investigates their equivalent widths, showing that while most ghostly systems are genuine DLAs, some are not.
AI.motivation: To provide an updated classification of PDLAs and a revised census of ghostly systems, and to investigate whether ghostly systems are always bona fide DLAs by measuring their absorption line equivalent widths.
AI.method: Updated classification of PDLAs; compilation of a revised catalogue of ghostly systems; measurement of equivalent widths of detected absorption lines in both stacked spectra and individual ghostly systems.
AI.result: The revised catalogue more than doubles the number of previously known ghostly system detections. Equivalent width measurements show that most ghostly systems are bona fide DLAs, but not all.
AI.conclusion: Ghostly systems are predominantly genuine DLAs, though exceptions exist, warranting further investigation into the nature of the non-DLA cases.
